name: AL-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: Terri Sewell is an incumbent in a district that leans Democratic by about ten points
Overwhelming fundraising edge: $3.75 million on hand versus roughly $116,000 for Ammie Akin
Prediction markets price Sewell's win probability near 98 percent

model.rationale: Sewell combines incumbency, a D+10 district, and a roughly thirteen-to-one cash advantage over Akin, while prediction markets price her near 98 percent; nothing in the available evidence suggests the seat is in play.
model.watch: A severe national Democratic collapse or an unexpected scandal involving Sewell could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat would still require a historic shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Terri Sewell seeks another term in a district anchored by Birmingham and the Black Belt that leans Democratic by about ten points, and she enters the general election with every structural advantage. She has raised nearly two million dollars and holds 3.75 million on hand, while Republican Ammie Akin has raised about 150 thousand. No public polls of the race are available, and no expert raters have flagged the contest as competitive. Prediction markets put Sewell's chances near 98 percent.

The fundamentals point the same direction: an incumbent running in a seat drawn to favor her party, in a year whose national environment adds only modest Republican lift. Akin would need an error of historic size to close a gap of this magnitude. The expected margin sits around twenty-one points, with Sewell heavily favored to win reelection.
